name: Mahāmudrā meditation (Kagyu)
method_summary: After the preliminaries and the guru's pointing-out, the meditator settles the mind (śamatha), looks directly at it (vipaśyanā), recognizes its empty and luminous nature, and sustains that recognition without contrivance or distraction in and between sessions, progressing through the four yogas.
signs_of_progress: experiences of bliss, clarity and non-thought (not to be clung to)
recognition of thoughts as mind's own display
the four yogas: one-pointedness, simplicity, one taste, non-meditation

warnings.text: The four deviations from emptiness and the three strayings into bliss, clarity and non-thought.
Without hope and fear the fruit is manifest; hope and fear themselves obstruct it.

notes: Not the haṭha 'mahāmudrā' seal (prc:mahamudra), which is a different practice with the same name.

name: Mahāmudrā śamatha with support
method_summary: The mind is rested on an object — a small pebble or stick, an image, the breath (counting or following), or a deity's form — without tightness or looseness, until it settles.

warnings.text: Too tight brings agitation, too loose dullness: balance them.

name: Mahāmudrā śamatha without support
method_summary: The mind rests without any object, letting thoughts subside in their own place, 'like waves returning to the ocean'.

name: Looking at the mind (Mahāmudrā vipaśyanā)

names.name: sems la lta ba; gnas 'gyu rig gsum

method_summary: In stillness and in movement the meditator looks for the mind: its colour, shape, location, where it arises, abides and goes, whether the still and moving mind are one or different; not finding anything, recognizes the unfindable, luminous nature.

equivalents.note: both are direct inquiries into the knower; the Advaita inquiry seeks the Self, the Kagyu looking finds no self and recognizes emptiness-clarity — the traditions insist on this difference

name: Cutting the root of mind (rtsad gcod)
method_summary: 'Cut the root of your own mind and leave awareness naked; let the muddy water of thought clear; neither stop nor create appearances, leave them in their own place' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā): decisive recognition that the thinking mind has no root, after which thoughts are no longer followed.
notes: Kagyu idiom; not to be confused with Dzogchen's trekchö (khregs chod, U45).

name: Resting uncontrived in ordinary mind
method_summary: Leaving the mind as it is, without recalling, anticipating, thinking, examining or controlling (Tilopa's six words), undistracted yet not fabricating — 'relax and rest in the uncontrived natural state'.
prerequisites: recognition of mind's nature through pointing-out

warnings.text: Resting without recognition becomes dull blankness; the manuals warn against mistaking a thought-free state for Mahāmudrā.

name: Receiving the pointing-out instruction
method_summary: The guru introduces the disciple directly to the nature of mind — in the manuals step by step: mind in stillness and movement, appearances as mind, mind as empty, emptiness as spontaneously present, and as self-liberated — and the disciple recognizes it by looking.

name: Carrying post-meditation onto the path
method_summary: Between sessions appearances are regarded as illusion and dream, thoughts recognized as they arise, and circumstances — including adversity — taken as path, until meditation and post-meditation are one taste.

name: The Kagyu preliminaries (ngöndro)
method_summary: Contemplation of the four thoughts, then the four special practices — refuge with prostrations and bodhicitta, Vajrasattva recitation, maṇḍala offering and guru yoga — each usually accumulated one hundred thousand times, as the ground for Mahāmudrā.
duration: commonly months to years; the hundred-thousand counts are the tradition's

name: Contemplating the four thoughts that turn the mind
method_summary: Reflecting in turn on the precious human life, death and impermanence, karma, and the suffering of saṃsāra until the mind turns from worldly concerns.

name: Refuge with prostrations
method_summary: Visualizing the refuge tree of the lineage, the practitioner recites the refuge prayer while performing full prostrations, joined with bodhicitta.

warnings.text: Physical prostrations should be adapted to the body's capacity (general teacher advice, not a text quotation).

name: Vajrasattva purification
method_summary: Visualizing Vajrasattva above the head and reciting his hundred-syllable mantra while nectar washes away negative karma and broken pledges, with the four powers of confession.

name: Maṇḍala offering
method_summary: Offering the universe arranged as a maṇḍala of heaps of grain on a plate, to accumulate merit.

name: Guru yoga
method_summary: Visualizing the guru as Vajradhara (in the Karma Kagyu, the Karmapa), supplicating with devotion, receiving the four empowerments as lights, and merging one's mind with the guru's; the most important of the preliminaries because realization comes through blessing.

equivalents.note: devotion to the teacher is common; guru yoga adds visualization, empowerment and mixing of minds

name: The Four-Session Guru Yoga of the 8th Karmapa
method_summary: A guru yoga recited in four sessions daily, supplicating the Karmapa as the union of all lineage gurus.

name: Invoking the Karmapa ('Karmapa khyenno')
method_summary: Repetition of the invocation 'Karmapa, think of me', a devotional mantra of the Karma Kagyu.

name: Recitation of oṃ maṇipadme hūṃ
method_summary: In Thangtong Gyalpo's practice the six-syllable mantra is recited while visualizing Avalokiteśvara purifying all beings.

name: Thangtong Gyalpo's Avalokiteśvara practice
method_summary: Refuge and bodhicitta; Avalokiteśvara visualized above oneself and all beings; light purifies; the six-syllable mantra; dissolution and resting with body, speech and mind as the deity's.

name: Arousing the thought of awakening (bodhicittotpāda)
method_summary: In the Jewel Ornament: generating aspiring and engaging bodhicitta in a ritual and training in its precepts.

name: Taking the bodhisattva vows (praṇidhāna)
method_summary: Taken in the Kagyu according to the Jewel Ornament's ritual of bodhicitta.

name: The Six Yogas of Nāropa
method_summary: A graded set of completion-stage practices received after empowerment: inner heat as foundation, then illusory body, dream, clear light, intermediate state and transference (with 'entering another's body'). Summary only: this ontology does not record methods.

warnings.text: If the fourfold application is not known, qualities may turn into faults; without the equal taste of the elements there is no progress; the armour of inner heat is essential.
Given to unfit vessels the instruction breaks the pledge and leads to hell.
The heedless, craving and intoxicated fall to lower realms.

name: Inner heat (gtum mo, caṇḍālī)
method_summary: Summary: a completion-stage yoga of the channels, winds and drops in which inner heat is kindled and the drops melt, giving rise to the four joys, bliss-warmth and non-conceptuality; the root ('main trunk') of the six yogas. No method details are recorded here.

equivalents.note: both raise an inner fire/energy through a central channel; the Buddhist practice aims at clear light and bliss-emptiness, not the union of Kuṇḍalinī and Śiva — the traditions keep them distinct

signs_of_progress: signs like warmth, smoke, fireflies, a lamp, and the sky; bliss; thoughts ceasing; hot and cold mixing (bka' dpe phyi ma)

warnings.text: If one does not know the fourfold application there is danger that qualities turn into faults; the remedies are countless; the armour of inner heat is important.
The breath-and-wind practice must be learned from the guru's mouth.

name: Illusory body yoga (sgyu lus)
method_summary: Seeing one's body, appearances and all beings as illusory — like a mirror image, a rainbow, the moon in water — first by contemplation and in daily life, then (in the completion stage) arising as the pure illusory body of the deity.
notes: The contemplative portion is not restricted; the completion-stage 'pure illusory body' depends on restricted wind practices.

name: Dream yoga (rmi lam)
method_summary: Setting the intention before sleep and watching with mindfulness, the practitioner recognizes dreams as dreams, then trains in them — increasing, transforming, emanating, travelling to pure lands — knows them as illusion, abandons fear, and meditates on suchness; recognition in dream prepares recognition in the bardo.

equivalents.note: the sūtra contemplation of phenomena as dreamlike is the waking basis of dream yoga

signs_of_progress: travelling to pure lands; riding sun and moon (Karṇatantravajrapada)

warnings.text: Miracles in dreams, if taken as real, become obstacles; known as illusion, they become path.

notes: U46 owns this id; U45 contributes the Nyingma/Bön forms.

name: Clear light yoga ('od gsal) and luminous sleep
method_summary: Recognizing the clear light in the gap between waking, sleep and dream and holding it through deep sleep ('awakening through deep sleep'), mixing day and night; its full form rests on restricted completion-stage wind practice.
signs_of_progress: signs of lights, rainbows, dawn, sun and moon (Ṣaḍdharmopadeśa)

name: Intermediate-state yoga (bar do)
method_summary: Training in the three bardos: inner heat and illusory body in life, dream yoga in sleep, and at death recognizing the clear light in the dissolution; failing that, arising as illusory body in the bardo, or blocking or choosing rebirth.

name: Transference of consciousness ('pho ba)
method_summary: Summary: at death (after training in life) consciousness is sent through the crown aperture to a pure land or merged with the guru's mind or the dharmakāya; the texts list many kinds. The Drikung Kagyu is known for phowa gatherings. No method details are recorded here.

equivalents.note: yogic departure through the crown at death in Hindu yoga; the Buddhist practice transfers consciousness to a pure land or dharmakāya, not a soul to Brahman

warnings.text: When the time has come, transfer; transferring at the wrong time kills the deities.
Transference is to be done when the signs of death appear, with joy and without attachment.

name: Entering another's body (grong 'jug)
method_summary: Summary: the transference of one's consciousness into a dead body, which it revives — 'casting off and taking up like a snake's skin'; by the tradition's account practised by Marpa's son Darma Dode and thereafter lost in Tibet. No method details are recorded.

equivalents.note: the Hindu yogic power of entering another body (the Śaṅkara legend, YS 3.38); the Kagyu presents it as a transference practice for others' benefit

warnings.text: Requires mastery over wind and mind and stability in both stages; a companion keeping the pledges is to be cherished.

name: Yantra exercises ('khrul 'khor)
method_summary: Summary: sets of physical movements combined with breath holding (in the Karṇatantravajrapada six root and thirty-nine branch exercises) used with inner heat to clear obstacles in the channels. No method details are recorded.

warnings.text: Improper practice of the wind yogas is taught to cause wind disorders; the exercises are learned only from a teacher (tradition's teaching; see obs:wind-disorder-from-practice).

name: The seven-point meditation posture

names.name: lus gnad bdun (the seven key points of body)

method_summary: Legs crossed, spine straight, hands in the meditation gesture below the navel, shoulders open, neck straightened, tongue and gaze settled; 'straighten like a plantain stem, cross like a lattice' (bka' dpe phyi ma).
notes: Usually called 'the seven points of Vairocana' in Tibetan manuals; the enumeration here is the common one (from memory), the bka' dpe phyi ma gives its own images.

name: Karmamudrā (consort practice)
method_summary: Kagyu contribution: in some lists one of Nāropa's dharmas, the 'method path'; sealed and restricted; summary only.

warnings.text: The heedless, those driven by craving, dependent on another and intoxicated fall from the meaning and again to the lower realms.
The method-path instruction is not given to all; it is sealed three times.

notes: U44 owns the Indian practice entry; this adds the Kagyu sources and warnings.

name: Niguma's six dharmas
method_summary: The Shangpa counterpart of the six yogas (inner heat, illusory body, dream, clear light, transference, bardo) as transmitted from Niguma; the root of the five golden dharmas. Summary only.

name: Amulet-box Mahāmudrā (Shangpa)
method_summary: Niguma's Mahāmudrā: after guru yoga, resting the mind uncontrived so that it is self-liberated, looking at thoughts so that they self-liberate, and letting the faults of deviation self-liberate.

name: The three integrations (Shangpa)
method_summary: In every activity the guru, the deity and illusion are carried onto the path.

name: White and red Khecarī (Shangpa)
method_summary: Deity practices of the white and red sky-goers, the 'flowers' of the five golden dharmas.

name: Deathless body and mind (Shangpa)
method_summary: The 'fruit' practices of the Shangpa, joining deity and wind yogas for the undying mind; summary only.

name: Sukhasiddhi's six dharmas (Shangpa)
method_summary: Instructions from Sukhasiddhi transmitted in the Shangpa alongside Niguma's; summary only.

name: The fivefold Mahāmudrā
method_summary: One session includes all five: arousing bodhicitta, arising as the yidam, guru devotion, resting in the Mahāmudrā view, and dedicating the merit with aspiration.

name: The six equal tastes (Drukpa)
method_summary: Meeting thoughts, afflictions, gods and demons, suffering, illness and death as one taste with the nature of mind, often in solitary or charnel places.

name: Cakrasaṃvara practice
method_summary: Kagyu contribution: the principal Kagyu yidam; his empowerment (the sixty-two-deity maṇḍala) opens the six dharmas; generation-stage practice precedes the completion stage.
notes: U44 owns the Indian Cakrasaṃvara practice; shared id.

name: Vajravārāhī practice
method_summary: The consort of Cakrasaṃvara as yidam (Vajrayoginī / Vajravārāhī, often in Nāropa's form); her fifteen-goddess empowerment 'indicated by symbol' ripens for the six dharmas.

name: Mahākāla protector practice (Kagyu)
method_summary: Daily and annual rituals to the protector — Bernagchen for the Karma Kagyu, six-armed Mahākāla for the Shangpa — to remove obstacles to practice.

name: Solitary mountain retreat (ri chos)
method_summary: Practice alone in caves and hermitages, renouncing worldly concerns — the model of Milarepa and of the Drukpa and Drikung retreatants at Kailash, Lapchi and Tsari.

warnings.text: Extreme austerity (Milarepa's nettle diet) is told as the exemplar's life, not prescribed as method.

name: The three-year retreat
method_summary: A closed group retreat of three years and about six weeks following a set curriculum (preliminaries, Mahāmudrā, six yogas of Nāropa and Niguma, deity practices), systematized by Jamgön Kongtrul and spread internationally by Kalu Rinpoche.
duration: three years and about six weeks

name: Singing songs of realization (mgur)
method_summary: Spontaneous or traditional vajra songs sung by teachers and practitioners, often at gaṇacakra feasts, as teaching and as expression of realization.
